_meta.description: SmartVoter LLM prompt templates. Edit here instead of in Python source. Each template uses {variable} placeholders filled by the provider at call time.

changelog.v1.1: Extracted to JSON; added dedicated root_question template with improved multilingual instructions
changelog.v1.2: Values-first redesign: root_question now elicits underlying values from everyday-life framing. Added follow_up_from_salience template. Updated generate_question_with_critique to connect policy to daily life.
changelog.v1.3: CRITICAL FIX: All question prompts now strictly require CLOSED YES/NO or AGREE/DISAGREE propositions. Open-ended questions ('What priorities...', 'How do you think...') are explicitly forbidden. Examples updated to only show correct closed-form questions. Salience-only forms ('How important is it that...') are also forbidden because they reveal no directional preference.

system_neutral: You are a neutral, non-partisan political analyst assistant for the SmartVoter app. Your job is to help users discover what they genuinely value — not just what they think they should support politically. You classify, summarize, and analyze political positions and legislative data for Israeli parties. Always be factual, balanced, and concise. Always respond with valid JSON only — no markdown fences, no extra text.

root_question.description: Generate a broad, values-revealing CLOSED question (agree/disagree) for a topic. Must be a clear proposition answerable on the Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale. NEVER open-ended.
root_question.user_message:
Generate a CLOSED, values-revealing survey question in English, Hebrew (עברית), and Russian for the SmartVoter political-preference app.

TOPIC (English): {topic_name_en}
TOPIC (Hebrew):  {topic_name_he}
TOPIC (Russian): {topic_name_ru}
TOPIC DESCRIPTION: {topic_description}

── MANDATORY QUESTION FORMAT ───────────────────────────────────────────
The question MUST be a CLOSED PROPOSITION — a statement or YES/NO question that a person AGREES or DISAGREES with on the Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale.

Think of it as: the user reads the question and thinks 'Yes, I support this' or 'No, I oppose this' — with degrees in between.

✅ CORRECT FORMATS:
   • 'Should the government [do X]?'
   • 'Do you support [proposition]?'
   • 'Should [group/institution] have the right to [action]?'
   • 'The state should [policy position].' (as a statement to agree/disagree with)

❌ FORBIDDEN — these CANNOT be answered on Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support:
   • 'What priorities should determine...?' (open-ended — no opposing pole)
   • 'How do you think the government should...?' (open-ended)
   • 'Which approach is best for...?' (choice question, not agree/disagree)
   • 'How important is it to you that...?' (measures salience, not direction — WRONG)
   • 'In your opinion, what should...?' (open-ended — no proposition to support or oppose)
   • ANY question starting with 'What', 'Which', 'How do', 'In your opinion' that does not contain a clear proposition

── CONTENT RULES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• The question must be a BROAD introduction to the topic — not about a specific law or event.
• Ground it in EVERYDAY LIFE: frame it around concrete concerns (food prices, military service equality, hospital waiting times, school costs, etc.).
• BOTH poles must represent legitimate positions: 'Strongly Oppose' AND 'Strongly Support' must both be positions a reasonable adult could genuinely hold.
• Do NOT name specific parties, politicians, specific bills, specific past events, or specific dates.
• The question must be answerable by someone who has NEVER followed Israeli politics.
• Hebrew must be natural right-to-left text. Russian must be natural — not a literal translation.

── CORRECT EXAMPLES BY TOPIC ───────────────────────────────────────────
For 'healthcare':
  ✅ 'Should the government significantly increase funding for public hospitals and clinics so that all citizens can access quality care without needing private health insurance?'
  ❌ 'What priorities should determine the government's approach to healthcare?' (FORBIDDEN — open-ended)
  ❌ 'How important is it to you that healthcare is affordable?' (FORBIDDEN — salience, not direction)

For 'cost_of_living':
  ✅ 'Should the government directly subsidize or control the prices of basic goods — such as food, housing, and utilities — to make them more affordable for ordinary families?'
  ❌ 'What should the government do about the cost of living?' (FORBIDDEN — open-ended)

For 'military_service':
  ✅ 'Should military service be mandatory and equal for ALL citizens, regardless of their religious background or group affiliation?'
  ❌ 'How do you think the burden of military service should be distributed?' (FORBIDDEN — open-ended)

For 'judiciary':
  ✅ 'Should an independent court system have the authority to strike down laws passed by an elected parliamentary majority, even when those laws have broad public support?'
  ❌ 'How important is it to you that the courts are independent?' (FORBIDDEN — salience, not direction)

For 'religion_state':
  ✅ 'Should religious authorities have the power to determine personal status decisions — such as who can marry whom — for all Israeli citizens?'
  ❌ 'To what extent should religion influence daily life?' (FORBIDDEN — open-ended, no clear proposition)

For 'economy_taxes':
  ✅ 'Should higher-income earners pay significantly more in taxes to fund public services and reduce inequality?'
  ❌ 'What approach should the government take to taxation and income inequality?' (FORBIDDEN)

── SELF-CHECK BEFORE OUTPUT ────────────────────────────────────────────
Before writing your answer, test the question:
  1. Can a person clearly say 'I support this' or 'I oppose this'? → If not, rewrite.
  2. Does 'Strongly Support' map to ONE specific policy direction? → If not, rewrite.
  3. Does 'Strongly Oppose' map to the OPPOSITE specific policy direction? → If not, rewrite.
  4. Does the question start with 'What', 'Which', 'How do', or 'In your opinion'? → REWRITE.
  5. Is it grounded in everyday life, not technical jargon? → If not, rewrite.

── OUTPUT FORMAT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Return JSON with ALL of these keys:
  question_en          (string — closed proposition in natural English),
  question_he          (string — natural Hebrew, right-to-left, NOT a literal translation),
  question_ru          (string — natural Russian, NOT a literal translation),
  context_note_en      (string — 1–2 neutral sentences explaining the real-life stakes for someone with no political background),
  answer_scale         (list of exactly 5 English strings, always: ['Strongly oppose', 'Somewhat oppose', 'Neutral / unsure', 'Somewhat support', 'Strongly support']),
  everyday_life_hook   (string — 1 concrete daily-life example, e.g. 'hospital copayments', 'military draft', 'Saturday opening hours'),
  neutrality_risk      ('low' | 'medium' | 'high'),
  loaded_terms         (list of strings — any potentially biased words; [] if none),
  is_loaded            (boolean — is the question biased or slanted?),
  bias_direction       (string or null — e.g. 'left', 'right', 'religious', 'secular'),
  suggested_revision   (string or null — improved neutral wording if is_loaded is true),
  reading_level        ('general public' | 'educated' | 'expert'),
  requires_context     (boolean),
  context_note         (string or null).

follow_up_from_salience.description: When a user has rated a topic as highly important, generate a targeted CLOSED follow-up question (agree/disagree) that drills into the specific policy aspect they care about most.
follow_up_from_salience.user_message:
Generate a targeted CLOSED FOLLOW-UP question for a topic the user already said is HIGHLY IMPORTANT to them.

TOPIC the user cares about: {topic_name_en}
TOPIC DESCRIPTION: {topic_description}
The user's previous answer indicated this topic is VERY IMPORTANT to them.

Available policy sub-items within this topic:
{policy_items_summary}

── MANDATORY QUESTION FORMAT ───────────────────────────────────────────
The question MUST be a CLOSED PROPOSITION answerable on the Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale.

✅ CORRECT: 'Should the government [specific approach] to solve [everyday problem]?'
✅ CORRECT: 'Do you believe private solutions are better than government intervention for [specific issue]?'
✅ CORRECT: A clear statement the user AGREES with or OPPOSES.

❌ FORBIDDEN:
   • 'Which approach is better for...?' (choice question, not agree/disagree)
   • 'What should be done about...?' (open-ended)
   • 'How do you think...?' (open-ended)
   • 'What is the best way to...?' (open-ended)
   • 'How important is...?' (salience, not direction)

── PURPOSE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
This follow-up should reveal WHICH SPECIFIC DIRECTION the user wants within the topic. For example, if the topic is 'cost_of_living' and the user said it's very important:
  → Does the user want DIRECT GOVERNMENT PRICE CONTROLS? Or MARKET COMPETITION AND TAX CUTS?
  These are two OPPOSING approaches that different parties represent — and the Strongly Support / Strongly Oppose poles must map exactly to these two directions.

── CONTENT RULES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Target one of the policy sub-items listed above — choose the one with the most discriminating party positions.
• Be more specific than the root question, but still accessible to non-political users.
• Both poles must represent LEGITIMATE political positions that actual voters hold.
• Do NOT name specific parties, politicians, or specific bills.
• Use concrete everyday language — no jargon.

── OUTPUT FORMAT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Return JSON with ALL of these keys:
  question_en          (string — closed proposition in natural English),
  question_he          (string — natural Hebrew),
  question_ru          (string — natural Russian),
  context_note_en      (string — 1–2 sentences on daily-life stakes),
  answer_scale         (list of exactly 5 English strings: ['Strongly oppose', 'Somewhat oppose', 'Neutral / unsure', 'Somewhat support', 'Strongly support']),
  policy_item_slug     (string — which of the provided policy slugs this question best targets),
  neutrality_risk      ('low' | 'medium' | 'high'),
  loaded_terms         (list of strings — [] if none),
  is_loaded            (boolean),
  bias_direction       (string or null),
  suggested_revision   (string or null),
  reading_level        ('general public' | 'educated' | 'expert'),
  requires_context     (boolean),
  context_note         (string or null).

generate_question_with_critique.description: Generate a policy-item-specific CLOSED question (agree/disagree) AND self-critique it in one call.
generate_question_with_critique.user_message:
Generate a neutral CLOSED survey question for the SmartVoter app AND immediately self-critique it — all in one JSON response.

Policy item: {title}
Description: {description}
Directional axis: {directional_axis}

── MANDATORY QUESTION FORMAT ───────────────────────────────────────────
The question MUST be a CLOSED PROPOSITION — a statement or YES/NO question that a user SUPPORTS or OPPOSES.

'Strongly Support' must clearly correspond to the POSITIVE pole of the directional axis.
'Strongly Oppose' must clearly correspond to the NEGATIVE pole of the directional axis.

✅ CORRECT QUESTION FORMATS:
   • 'Should the government [action matching positive/negative axis pole]?'
   • 'Do you support [clear policy proposition]?'
   • 'Should [institution] have the power to [action]?'

❌ FORBIDDEN FORMATS — these CANNOT be placed on a Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale:
   • 'What should be the government's approach to [topic]?' (no proposition to oppose)
   • 'How should [policy area] be handled?' (open-ended)
   • 'What priorities should determine [policy]?' (open-ended)
   • 'How do you think [institution] should work?' (open-ended)
   • 'Which approach is better: [A] or [B]?' (choice, not position)
   • 'How important is [outcome] to you?' (salience only — reveals no policy direction)
   • ANY question starting with: 'What', 'Which approach', 'How do', 'How should', 'In your opinion'

── SELF-CHECK ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Before finalising the question, verify:
  1. Can someone clearly say 'I support this' or 'I oppose this'? If not → REWRITE.
  2. Does Strongly Support map directly to the POSITIVE axis pole? If not → REWRITE.
  3. Does Strongly Oppose map directly to the NEGATIVE axis pole? If not → REWRITE.
  4. Does the question start with a forbidden word/phrase? → REWRITE.

── CONTENT RULES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Frame the question in CONCRETE EVERYDAY TERMS — not legislative jargon.
• Both poles must represent positions a reasonable adult could genuinely hold.
• Do NOT name specific parties, politicians, or specific pieces of legislation.
• Must be answerable without knowledge of Israeli politics.
• Include a 1–2 sentence context_note_en explaining the real-life stakes.
• Hebrew and Russian must be natural — not word-for-word translations.

── SELF-CRITIQUE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
After generating the question, evaluate:
- Is it truly closed (not open-ended)? Can it be placed on a Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale?
- Is the wording loaded toward one political side?
- Does it require knowledge of specific events, scandals, or legislation?

Return JSON with ALL of these keys:
  question_en (string — closed proposition in natural English),
  question_he (string — natural Hebrew),
  question_ru (string — natural Russian),
  context_note_en (string — 1–2 sentences on everyday-life stakes),
  everyday_life_example (string — 1 concrete example of how this affects real people),
  answer_scale (list of 5 English strings),
  neutrality_risk (low|medium|high),
  loaded_terms (list of strings, empty if none),
  source_refs (list of strings),
  is_loaded (boolean),
  bias_direction (string or null),
  suggested_revision (string or null — only if is_loaded=true),
  reading_level (general public|educated|expert),
  requires_context (boolean),
  context_note (string or null).

generate_question.description: Generate a neutral, CLOSED policy-item-specific question (agree/disagree) in three languages.
generate_question.user_message:
Generate a neutral, non-partisan CLOSED survey question in English, Hebrew (עברית), and Russian for the SmartVoter app.

Policy item: {title}
Description: {description}
Directional axis: {directional_axis}

── MANDATORY QUESTION FORMAT ───────────────────────────────────────────
The question MUST be a CLOSED PROPOSITION that the user can SUPPORT or OPPOSE.
• Strongly Support = agrees with the POSITIVE pole of the directional axis
• Strongly Oppose = agrees with the NEGATIVE pole of the directional axis

✅ CORRECT: 'Should the government [policy action]?'
✅ CORRECT: 'Do you support [clear policy proposal]?'
❌ FORBIDDEN: 'What should be done about [topic]?' (open-ended — no proposition)
❌ FORBIDDEN: 'How do you think [policy area] should work?' (open-ended)
❌ FORBIDDEN: 'How important is [outcome] to you?' (salience question — no direction)
❌ FORBIDDEN: 'What priorities should determine [policy]?' (open-ended)
Any question starting with 'What', 'Which approach', 'How do', 'How should' must be REWRITTEN as a closed proposition.

── CONTENT RULES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Frame in concrete everyday language — not legislative jargon.
• Both poles must represent legitimate positions real people hold.
• Do not name specific parties, politicians, or specific legislation.
• Must be answerable without knowing Israeli politics.
• Include a 1–2 sentence context note on real-life impact.
• Hebrew and Russian must be natural — not literal translations.

Return JSON with:
  question_en (string),
  question_he (string, Hebrew),
  question_ru (string, Russian),
  context_note_en (string, 1–2 sentences on daily-life impact),
  answer_scale (list of 5 English strings),
  neutrality_risk (low|medium|high),
  loaded_terms (list of strings, empty if none),
  source_refs (list of strings).

critique_question.description: Critically review a question for two issues: (1) bias/loaded wording, and (2) whether it is a closed proposition answerable on Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale.
critique_question.user_message:
Critically review this survey question for TWO types of problems:
  1. BIAS or LOADED WORDING
  2. WHETHER IT IS A CLOSED PROPOSITION (can it be answered on a Strongly Oppose → Strongly Support scale?)

Question: {question}

A question is VALID only if it is a CLOSED PROPOSITION — a statement or yes/no question where:
  - 'Strongly Support' maps to one clear policy direction
  - 'Strongly Oppose' maps to the OPPOSITE policy direction

A question is INVALID (open-ended) if it:
  - Starts with 'What priorities...', 'How do you think...', 'Which approach...', 'In your opinion...'
  - Asks about priorities or importance without stating a proposition ('How important is it that...')
  - Gives no opposing pole to take a stand on

Return JSON with:
  is_loaded (boolean — is the wording biased?),
  is_open_ended (boolean — is the question open-ended rather than a closed proposition?),
  bias_direction (string or null — 'left'|'right'|'religious'|'secular'|etc.),
  suggested_revision (string or null — ALWAYS provide a closed-form revision if is_open_ended is true),
  reading_level (string — 'general public'|'educated'|'expert'),
  requires_context (boolean),
  context_note (string or null — suggested context explanation).

summarize_bill_or_vote.description: Summarize an Israeli legislative item for SmartVoter.
summarize_bill_or_vote.user_message:
Summarize the following Israeli legislative item for the SmartVoter app.

Title: {title}
Text: {text}
Metadata: {metadata}

Return JSON with these exact keys:
  plain_summary (string, max 3 sentences, plain language),
  main_policy_change (string, 1 sentence),
  affected_groups (list of strings),
  is_procedural (boolean),
  importance_score (float 0.0–1.0),
  reasoning_summary (string, max 2 sentences, public explanation only — no chain-of-thought).

classify_and_extract.description: Classify a policy item into topics AND extract its directional axis in one call.
classify_and_extract.user_message:
Analyze this Israeli policy item and return BOTH topic classification AND directional policy axis in a single JSON response.

Title: {title}
Description: {description}

Available topics: {topics_list}

Return JSON with ALL of these keys:
  topics (list of objects with 'topic' and 'confidence' float 0–1),
  primary_topic (string from available topics),
  classification_confidence (float 0–1),
  axis_name (snake_case identifier for the policy axis),
  negative_pole (string — what -1 means on this axis),
  positive_pole (string — what +1 means on this axis),
  direction_explanation (string — 1 sentence explaining scale direction).

classify_policy_item.description: Classify an Israeli policy item into topics.

extract_policy_axis.description: Extract the directional policy axis for an Israeli political issue.
extract_policy_axis.user_message:
Extract the directional policy axis for this Israeli political issue.

Title: {title}
Description: {description}

Return JSON with:
  axis_name (snake_case identifier),
  negative_pole (string — what -1 means),
  positive_pole (string — what +1 means),
  direction_explanation (string — 1 sentence explaining scale direction).
